Lead Time Performance

Lead Time

Actual lead time = sample submission actual date minus colour & quality (swatch) receive date. If there is no swatch date, the document receive date is used. Calendar days. Target comes from the standard below.

Development Database

Works like Excel. Click a cell and type. Enter, Tab and the arrow keys move. F2 or double-click edits. Delete clears. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy and paste with Excel. Ctrl+D fills down. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo. Right-click for more. Every change is saved at once and written to the change log.
fx
All changes saved

Import Supplier Files

Choose one or more supplier development charts. Columns are matched by header name. Colours in one cell are split into one row each. Nothing is written until you confirm. A record missing from a new file is never deleted.
Drop .xlsx files here or
.xlsx and .xls. Several files at once is fine. When two files hold the same row, the newer file wins.

Preview

Import history

Supplier Email

Prepare request emails for the seasonal development chart. Nothing is sent from here. "Office 365" opens a draft in Outlook on the web (it is kept in your Drafts folder) and downloads the file to attach. "Mail app" opens a draft in Outlook desktop. "Download draft (.eml)" saves a draft with the file already attached: open it and Outlook shows the draft.

Suppliers

New supplier: first email only. Not saved to My Suppliers List. The draft carries the blank template.

Message

My Suppliers List

Who gets your development chart emails, and what every draft carries: default CC, wording and signature. Used by Supplier Email. Nothing is sent from here. The list opens locked; unlock it to change anything, lock it again when done.

Backup & Restore

A snapshot is taken automatically before every import, bulk change, delete and restore. Snapshots live in this browser. A backup file is the only way to move data to another computer.
